title: Best UGC Video Creators (2026): How to Hire One That Converts
description: Our picks of proven UGC video creators, plus a practical guide to briefing, usage rights and red flags before you order.
intro: User-generated content (UGC) videos look like a real customer talking about your product, which is exactly why they work in ads. The hard part is finding a creator who can deliver that on a deadline. Below are our current picks, followed by the checklist we use to judge a UGC gig.

faq.a: A short video, usually filmed on a phone, in which a creator uses or talks about your product the way a real customer would. Brands use them as organic social posts and, more often, as paid ads.

faq.q: Do I own the video after I order it?
faq.a: Not automatically. Usage rights depend on the gig. Many creators list commercial use or paid-ad rights as a separate extra. Confirm in writing, before you pay, where you may run the video and for how long.

faq.q: Do I have to ship my product to the creator?
faq.a: For physical products, usually yes. Ask whether the creator returns it and who pays shipping. For apps and websites, creators can film their own screen and phone instead.

faq.q: How many revisions should I expect?
faq.a: Each package states a revision count. Ask what counts as a revision: re-editing existing footage is normal, while a full reshoot often costs extra.

faq.q: Why hire through a marketplace instead of contacting a creator directly?
faq.a: The marketplace holds your payment until the order is completed, keeps seller reviews public, and offers a resolution process if something goes wrong.
